sections.title: Taxonomy and life cycle
sections.text: Puccinia poarum E. Nielsen (1877) is a microscopic rust fungus in the family Pucciniaceae, order Pucciniales (Basidiomycota). It has a macrocyclic, heteroecious life cycle, alternating five spore-producing stages between two hosts. Pycnia (spermogonia) and aecia develop on coltsfoot (Tussilago farfara); uredinia and telia develop on grasses in the genus Poa. Teliospores from the grasses germinate and produce basidiospores that infect coltsfoot; aeciospores formed there then infect a grass. Experimental inoculations document Poa pratensis and P. trivialis in particular.

sections.title: Symptoms on coltsfoot
sections.text: On Tussilago farfara, infection can produce round, thickened or gall-like leaf areas, yellow to orange and sometimes edged in purplish red, occasionally with a hole at the centre. The lower leaf surface bears groups of orange to orange-red aecia in small cups, with pycnia also present depending on the stage. The upper and lower surfaces therefore show different signs. These are the fungus’s reproductive structures, not mushroom caps. Another rust, Coleosporium tussilaginis, also occurs on coltsfoot but does not produce the same galls.

sections.title: Stages on grasses and identification limits
sections.text: On Poa, the uredinial and telial stages form pustules mainly on leaves: uredinia are yellow and powdery, while telia become brown. Their position varies with stage and account; one field source reports uredinia mainly on the upper surface and telia mainly below. Identifications made from a grass alone are difficult and may require microscopic examination. The taxonomy of rusts on Poa is complex: a German Red List notes that some older records of P. poarum on Poa reflect a broad species concept that included the P. poae-nemoralis group. Grass host records should therefore be interpreted cautiously.

sections.title: Use and caution
sections.text: This is a plant-parasitic fungus, with no food use documented in the sources consulted. This profile describes its life cycle and symptoms; it does not replace phytopathological expertise for identifying a specimen or diagnosing a plant.

traits: Microscopic rust in the Pucciniaceae; Puccinia poarum E. Nielsen, published in 1877
Macrocyclic, heteroecious life cycle with five spore stages on two hosts
Pycnia and aecia on coltsfoot (Tussilago farfara); orange to orange-red cup-shaped aecia on thickened leaf galls
Round yellow to orange, sometimes purplish-edged spots on coltsfoot; the two leaf surfaces show different signs
Yellow powdery uredinia and brown telia on Poa grasses, including P. pratensis and P. trivialis in experimental inoculations
Rusts on Poa can be difficult to assign to P. poarum because of a taxonomic complex and historically broad species concepts
Plant-parasitic fungus; no food use documented here
safetyNote: This rust fungus parasitizes plants. The illustrated symptoms alone are not sufficient to confirm an identification or plant-health diagnosis; stages on grasses may require microscopic examination.
